operativeSourceText:
(b) Section 2.05(2)(c) of the Credit Agreement is hereby
amended and restated in its entirety with the following:
(c) If, after giving effect to all mandatory prepayments of Term
Loans to the extent required by Sections 2.05(2)(a), (b) and (d), the Borrower and its Subsidiaries has (i) unrestricted cash on hand as of the last day of any calendar month in an amount that is greater than $50 million, the Borrower
shall, as soon as is reasonably practicable, but in any event no later than five (5) Business Days after the last day of such calendar month, prepay, or cause to be prepaid, an aggregate principal amount of Super-Priority Revolving Loans equal
to the lesser of (x) the aggregate principal amount of Super-Priority Revolving Loans then-outstanding and (y) the amount necessary to cause the amount of unrestricted cash on hand of the Borrower and its Subsidiaries as of the last day of
such recently ended calendar month to be less than or equal to $50 million and (ii) after giving effect to any mandatory prepayment pursuant to clause (i) above, Maintenance Liquidity as of the last day of any calendar month that is
greater than $115 million, the Borrower shall, as soon as is reasonably practicable, but in any event no later than five (5) Business Days after the last day of such calendar month, prepay, or cause to be prepaid, an aggregate principal
amount of Term Loans of any Class or Classes (in each case, as directed by the Borrower) to the extent necessary to cause Maintenance Liquidity as calculated as of the last day of such recently ended calendar month to be less than or equal to
$115 million; provided, however, if, on or prior to the date that is thirty days after the last day of the calendar month most recently ended, the Borrower obtains knowledge that Maintenance Liquidity was miscalculated for the last day of such
calendar month, and as a result, an amount that was otherwise required to be prepaid under this Section 2.05(2)(c)(ii) was not prepaid (such amount, the “Deficiency Amount”), no Default or Event of Default shall occur (or be
deemed to have occurred and be continuing) as a result of the Borrower’s failure to prepay the Deficiency Amount pursuant to this Section 2.05(2)(c)(ii) (or give notice thereof) so long as (x) the Deficiency Amount is less than
$1,300,000, and (y) within 5 Business Days of obtaining knowledge of such Deficiency Amount the Borrower makes a prepayment of such Deficiency Amount in accordance with this Section 2.05(2)(c)(ii). For the avoidance of doubt, if after any
recalculation of Maintenance Liquidity, the calculation of Maintenance Liquidity is lower than the amount most recently reported to the Administrative Agent, and therefore the mandatory prepayment that was made was higher than would have been
required at such time, the Administrative Agent shall be under no obligation to refund any overpayment amounts

findings.sourceEvidence: For the avoidance of doubt, if after any recalculation of Maintenance Liquidity, the calculation of Maintenance Liquidity is lower than the amount most recently reported to the Administrative Agent, and therefore the mandatory prepayment that was made was higher than would have been required at such time, the Administrative Agent shall be under no obligation to refund any overpayment amounts
findings.sourceCitation: Section 2.05(2)(c) (final sentence, 'for the avoidance of doubt' clause)
findings.proposedIrEvidence: No rule, exception, or definition in the proposed IR represents this clause; rules[1] (the r2 Maintenance Liquidity sweep) is marked sufficiency: COMPLETE with only one exception (the Deficiency Amount safe harbor for under-prepayment).
findings.verifierReasoning: This sentence is an independently operative provision that establishes a specific legal consequence distinct from the Deficiency Amount safe harbor: it forecloses any right of the Borrower to demand a refund from the Administrative Agent where a subsequent recalculation shows Maintenance Liquidity was actually lower (and thus the mandatory prepayment made was larger than strictly required). This affects a real economic/legal right (no refund obligation on overpayment) that a competent reviewer would want represented, particularly because the two rules that are compiled are both marked sufficiency: COMPLETE, which implies nothing further from the source was left unrepresented. A hypothetical: if the Borrower overpays under the ML sweep because its initial calculation was wrong (too high), and later recalculates ML as lower, the source is explicit the Agent has no refund obligation - the proposed IR contains nothing addressing this scenario at all, so a user relying on the IR alone would not know this outcome is foreclosed.

findings.proposedIrEvidence: calculationExpression: ADD(SUBTRACT(aggregate commitments under Super-Priority Revolving Credit Facility, ADD(outstanding revolving loans, LC face amount)), Adjustment to Liquidity from Monthly Factoring Report, unrestricted cash and Cash Equivalents) - sufficiency marked COMPLETE
findings.verifierReasoning: The proposed IR asserts a detailed, multi-term formula for 'Maintenance Liquidity' and marks it sufficiency: COMPLETE, but the only source text given for this review (Section 2(b)) never states this definition, no context items were retrieved, and Phase 2 explicitly flagged an unresolved dependency for lack of an anchoring structural node. I cannot verify from anything provided whether this formula is accurate, partially accurate, or fabricated. Given that this defined term is the linchpin of the $115 million sweep in rule r2, an incorrect or unsupported formula here would silently change the calculated prepayment amount without any visible flag, and the confident COMPLETE marking is exactly the kind of claim that deserves the most scrutiny under these instructions. I am flagging this as UNCERTAIN because I lack the evidence to confirm or refute the formula's correctness, but the provenance gap itself is real and should be surfaced.

findings.proposedIrEvidence: definitionId ir-definition:3e01409d96ff978c24e82d38, termName 'Deficiency Amount', calculationExpression: null, sufficiency: COMPLETE
findings.verifierReasoning: The source defines 'Deficiency Amount' by reference to the shortfall between the amount that was required to be prepaid under clause (c)(ii) and the amount actually prepaid - i.e., it is a computable quantity (required prepayment minus actual prepayment), not merely a label. The proposed IR leaves calculationExpression as null while still marking the definition's sufficiency as COMPLETE, which is an internally inconsistent posture: either the formula should be represented (even as a reference to the shortfall from rule r2's capacityExpression) or the sufficiency should not be COMPLETE. This could matter if a downstream consumer relies on the Deficiency Amount definition to compute the $1,300,000 threshold test and finds no calculable expression despite the COMPLETE flag.

I find no support for treating this as an actual wrong-threshold error; the underlying dollar amounts are faithfully and correctly represented.
